Q: Lag increasing for Slot created by debezium kafka connect A:

Since you clarified the Kafka topic is receiving row changes, then the connector is clearly fetching data from PostgreSQL. In that case the problem is not “it doesn’t fetch data”; the more likely problem is that it is not advancing feedback back to PostgreSQL fast enough, so confirmed_flush_lsn does not move and WAL keeps accumulating.

With your config, the two main causes are:

  • You only capture one table, while WAL is generated for the whole database. If that table is relatively low-traffic, Debezium may not commit offsets often enough.

  • heartbeat.interval.ms is not set. Heartbeats are the usual fix for this, because they let Debezium periodically commit progress even when business-table traffic is sparse.

A second possibility is a long-running transaction: if restart_lsn stays far behind confirmed_flush_lsn, PostgreSQL is likely being forced to retain old WAL for that transaction.

I would first start with enabling heartbeat

"heartbeat.interval.ms": "5000"

And then check for long-running transactions with pg_stat_activity if restart_lsn remains far behind confirmed_flush_lsn.

References:
https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/connectors/cc-postgresql-cdc-source-v2-debezium/cc-postgresql-cdc-source-v2-debezium.html
https://docs.confluent.io/kafka-connectors/debezium-postgres-source/current/postgres_source_connector_config.html

Q: Windows Terminal - open new tab with current environment A:

I came here with this same question, and was surprised to find there weren't any answers. I wonder if wt has been changed/improved since this was asked as I eventually found the following works:

wt -w 0 nt --inheritEnvironment

This starts a new tab in the current terminal session, with the same environment as the tab it is run in.

Note that the capital E is necessary.

Note also that it starts in a different directory. You can set that as well:

wt -w 0 nt --inheritEnvironment -d c:\users\public
wt -w 0 nt --inheritEnvironment -d %cd%

Q: Products search with correct and wrong input search term A:

That's not a simple search at all. You need an algorithm (similar to spell checking) to "fix" the incorrect parameters. One way is to calculate the similarity between the value and all correct values, and pick the closest ones. There are a lot of similarity algorithms. Some calculate how many letters differ in the same position. Others calculate swaps or deletions as well. You should look for terms like "Fuzzy search" or "Edit distance" or "Levenshtein distance".

The Smart Components project uses similarity algorithms to detect which values are closest. Some databases have functions that can calculate similarities. For example, SQL Server 2025 added functions that calculate similarities.

Q: nvidia-docker : Unknown runtime specified nvidia A:

Just running this was enough for me:

nvidia-ctk runtime configure
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart docker

Q: Set content of HTML <span> with Javascript A:

Now there's setHTML():

document.querySelector("span").setHTML("hello from <code>setHTML()</code>");
<span>this content will be overwritten</span>

The advantage this has over .innerHTML is that it sanitizes the content, mitigating cross-site scripting attacks. As a result, interactive elements like forms, inputs and buttons are silently removed by default. A Sanitizer should be defined to allow these:

const html = `
  <button>hello from setHTML()</button>
  <p>this won't show up because 'p' is not in the 'elements' array below</p>
`;

document.querySelector("span").setHTML(html, {
  sanitizer: new Sanitizer({elements: ["button"]})
});
<span>this content will be overwritten</span>
